title: Solitons in the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with the pseudo-Raman term, anti-diffusion gain and nonlinear loss
authors: Evgeny M. Gromov, Boris A. Malomed
abstract: We introduce a nonconservative nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) which includes additional nonlinear terms accounting for the pseudo-stimulated-Raman-scattering (pseudo-SRS) effect and cubic loss. An essentially novel feature of the model is the linear anti-diffusion gain, which leads to the obvious blow-up in the infinite or spatially periodic system. We consider the absorptive boundary conditions, which suppress the blow-up driven by effective convective instability in the setup. The NSLE model is derived, in the extended adiabatic approximation, from the underlying Zakharov system, which includes the viscosity term acting on its low-frequency component and the anti-diffusion gain in the high-frequency (HF) one. The latter term appears if the expansion, with respect to the deviation of the wavenumber, is performed not around the minimum-loss point (as in the usual situation), but around a maximum-loss point. Dynamics of moving solitons in the model is addressed by means of analytical and numerical methods. The sech approximation for the soliton predicts it as a stable fixed point (FP) of the system of balance equations for the HF norm and wave momentum, derived in the moving reference frame. The FP attraction basin is identified too. The predictions are corroborated by direct simulations of the full NSLE with the absorptive boundary conditions.
summary: This paper analyzes solitons in a complex, nonconservative Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation featuring pseudo-Raman scattering, cubic loss, and anti-diffusion gain. By reducing the dynamics to a fixed-point analysis, the authors predict the existence of stable soliton states. The results are confirmed by numerical simulations, demonstrating how the system's stability depends critically on the balance between its various nonlinear and gain/loss terms.
main_problem: The paper investigates the existence and dynamics of solitons within a nonconservative Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation (NLSE) that incorporates pseudo-Raman scattering, cubic loss, and a novel anti-diffusion gain term.
main_result: The analysis predicts that stable soliton solutions exist, corresponding to a stable fixed point (FP) in the derived dynamical system, provided the initial conditions fall within a specific attraction basin.
method: The study employs a combination of analytical techniques, including the $	ext{sech}$ ansatz and reduction to coupled balance equations, alongside direct numerical simulations of the full nonconservative NLSE.
model_or_system: The model is an NLSE derived from the Zakharov system, extended to include pseudo-SRS effects and cubic loss. A key feature is the linear anti-diffusion gain, which necessitates the use of absorptive boundary conditions to prevent blow-up.
key_observables: Soliton amplitude, wave momentum, and the stability/location of the fixed point (FP) in the reduced dynamical system.
important_parameters: The relationship between nonlinear-loss and anti-diffusion-gain coefficients ($\sigma$), which dictates the nature of the fixed point (e.g., stable spiral vs. center-type).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of the extended adiabatic approximation for deriving the NLSE, and the use of absorptive boundary conditions to manage the inherent blow-up tendency from the anti-diffusion gain.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase-plane trajectories showing attraction to the stable fixed point or decay, and direct simulations confirm stable soliton propagation when initial conditions match the predicted FP values.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the complex nonconservative NLSE model, then deriving the reduced dynamical system using analytical approximations, and finally corroborating the theoretical predictions through detailed numerical simulations.
why_interesting: This work extends the standard soliton framework by incorporating multiple dissipative and gain terms (pseudo-SRS, cubic loss, anti-diffusion gain), making it highly relevant to advanced quantum optics and nonlinear wave physics.
